project_name: Nodiac Adrian Township modular data center
status_detail: Nodiac project page describes a proposed small modular data center in Adrian Township, Monroe County with 12 MW target capacity and a 1-3 acre footprint; local reporting says Nodiac presented the plan to Adrian Township in June 2026 and county later considered/approved an 18-month moratorium on data centers.
notes: Developer source is live and specific; Monroe County Herald snippets identify Nodiac's Director of Development and a 12-MW plan, plus county moratorium action. Treat status as planned/early permit process, not approved.

status_detail: DCD reported Wrightstown would hold a referendum after discussions with Cloverleaf about rezoning land for a data center development of up to 1 GW; NBC26 reported internal emails with Cloverleaf but the village administrator said no formal or informal proposal had been brought before the board/staff and zoning did not allow a large-scale data center at that time.
notes: Wrightstown spans Brown and Outagamie counties; some trackers classify this prospect as Brown County, but it is included here because the village also includes Outagamie County territory and the county batch requires broad capture. Status is early prospect; no formal application/site identified in cited reports.

aliases: Port Washington Lighthouse Data Center Campus
status_detail: Wisconsin DNR says Vantage is developing a data center campus in Port Washington, Ozaukee County and lists active permits/approvals; Vantage states the 672-acre campus will include four data centers totaling 902 MW and 2.5M square feet, scheduled for completion in 2028. The city project site says construction began in December 2025.
notes: OpenAI and Oracle are announced partners/tenants for the Stargate campus; DNR page confirms permitting, Ozaukee County location, and construction-related approvals.

project_name: Metered Mining Hager City data center
status_detail: Dairyland Power economic development page reports Pierce Pepin Cooperative Services and SwiftCurrent Connect celebrated a new data center in Hager City with Metered Mining in July 2024; Wisconsin Electric Cooperative News reports the June 24 ribbon cutting, initial 1 MW growing to potential 20 MW, and later 4.5 MW load after about a year.
notes: Capacity recorded as 20 MW potential buildout based on co-op trade reporting; article also reports 4.5 MW actual draw after roughly one year. Facility supports AI/data analytics/VR/cryptocurrency workloads.
